Q: How to set up a constraint on a column for a value to be greater than a number? A:

CHECK constraints

A CHECK constraint enforces a SQL expression as a condition on the values that can be inserted into or updated in one or more columns of a table. For example, a CHECK constraint might ensure that the quantity column in a table only contains values that are greater than zero or that the salary column in a table only contains values in a specific range.

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE persons(
    person_email VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY,
    age INTEGER CHECK (age>0)
);

INSERT INTO persons(person_email, age) VALUES ('aaa', -1);

Operation on table TESTDB.PUBLIC.PERSONS failed because CHECK constraint "SYS_CONSTRAINT_f...7", which requires that age>0, was violated

Q: what's a good functional language for someone coming from perl? A:

OCaml, high performance, fast prototyping like Perl, and great ecosystem (OPAM, Dune, libraries for everything). I spent a few years ramping up a Perl team on OCaml and most of them found it tickle the same brain itch that Perl did.

Some of my favorite features are:

  • Type system so good that you forget it's there
  • Algebraic data types
  • Immutable by default, but can mutate if you need to
  • Fast iteration with utop
